full_judgment:
Tariq-ul-Hakim J: This Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order of sanction dated 15-9-1998 according permission by the respondent No. 3 for prosecuting the petitioner in Metro Special Case No. 178 of 1999 arising out of Motijheel PS case No. 103 dated 17-10-1996 under sections 420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947) pending in the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka as contained in Annexure-C should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. It is stated that on 17-10-1996 one AKM Feroz Mia, Anti-Corruption Officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, lodged a First Information Report with the Motijheel Police Station against the petitioner and 3 others namely, Anwarul Alam, former Chairman of Rajuk, Lt Col (Retd) Md Nurul Hoque, Member, Land and Estate Rajuk and Mohammad Ullah, former Assistant Director Estate, Rajuk, Dhaka stating, inter alia, that the above named accused persons in collaboration with each other misused their power and allotted 9 kathas and 24 square feet of land in exchange of 3 kathas of land in Uttara Model Town for financial benefit of Taka 47 lac. Thereafter, on the basis of the said FIR Motijheel PS case No. 103 dated 17-10-1996 under sections 420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947) was started against the accused persons. Subsequently, the Anti-Corruption Bureau after investigation of the case submitted charge sheet No. 782 dated 24-9-1998 under section 420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947) against the petitioner and 3 others. After submission of charge sheet the case were referred to the office of the Hon'ble Prime Minister of the Government of Bangladesh for according sanction as per provisions of section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 for prosecuting the accused persons. The office of the Hob'ble Prime Minister under the signature of the respondent No.3 communicated the, Government sanction to prosecute the petitioner and at the same time directed that the other 3 accused persons be made witnesses in the same case. 

 11. The sanction to prosecute constitutes a condition precedent for the prosecution and the Government has absolute discretion to grant or withhold such sanction but the sanctioning authority is to see that the facts alleged disclose a prima facie case against the persons sought to be prosecuted. Although it has a discretion to refuse sanction on any ground. However, when sanction is accorded to prosecute a person it must be based on materials on record placed before it failing which the sanction will be invalid and the trial Court will not have the jurisdiction to prosecute him and the said defect cannot be subsequently cured. This finds support from the decisions in Syed Mustafizur Rahman vs State reported in 53 DLR 125 as well as the case of Abdul Hakim vs State and Alfazuddin vs. State reported in 45 DLR 352. In the instant case in the order of sanction (Annexure-C to the Writ Petition) it has not been stated on what materials the sanctioning authority was satisfied to accord sanction to prosecute the petitioner. Furthermore, it has also not been stated what extraneous materials and evidence was placed before the sanctioning authority to make it aware of the guilt of the petitioner for which sanction was sought and subsequently accorded. Further, in the sanction order there is no mention what pecuniary advantage was obtained by the petitioner and what papers were placed before the sanctioning authority which convinced the sanctioning authority that the alleged offence was committed by the petitioner. This indicates that the sanction was a mere mechanical formality which is no sanction in the eye of law and therefore no sanction at all. 

 15. Accordingly, this Rule is made absolute and the impugned order of sanction dated 15-9-1998 according permission by the Government to prosecute the petitioner in Metro Special Case No. 178 of 1999 arising out of Motjiheel PS case No. 103 dated 17-10-1996 under sections 420/1 09 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947) pending in the Court of the Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka as contained in Annexure C is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 16. All further proceedings of Metro Special Case No. 178 of 1999 arising out of Motijheel PS case No. 103 dated 17-10-1996 under section 420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947) pending in the Court of the Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka as contained in Annexure-C is declared illegal and without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
